findings.reason: §2's scope and its done-when are written against a resolver that does not exist, and an implementer told "that is the new work" will fork roadmap's resolution rather than extend it.
findings.text: §2 says `plan-section-depends-on` entries "become edges for the first time, and that is the new work", but `_section_scoped_edges` already parses every entry through `parse_plan_ref`, resolves the `project:`-qualified form against the named mount, judges satisfaction through `_section_satisfied` and `declared_section_identities`, refuses malformed refs through `section_dependency_refusals`, and emits `dangling-hard-dependency`; the true new work is only lifting the resolved edges into the plan-level closure (`longest_path` at roadmap.py:3426, `unlocks` at roadmap.py:3324), not building resolution; the same omission covers `_plan_section_deps` (roadmap.py:409), `_gate_section_edges` (roadmap.py:302) and `_after_edges` (roadmap.py:987), which are the three edge sources §2 describes as if unbuilt

findings.reason: naming the owner turns §4 into an extension of one classifier instead of a third call site, and removes the wrong premise that parity does not already exist.
findings.text: §4 says a section row's runs carry "one classification each, taken from the same function `crew live` calls", but names no function: the owner is `partition_live_runs` (reckon/mcp_views.py:1860), which already delegates to `classify_pointer` (reckon/crew/recovery.py) and already asserts in its docstring that "the roadmap, the sprint view and `recover` cannot disagree"; §4's premise that the surfaces "can no longer disagree" is therefore already true at plan level, and the real delta is extending `_run_row`/`_run_target_plan` from plan to `plan#section`

findings.reason: four parallel derivations of one roadmap payload is exactly the drift §4's own parity test exists to prevent, and the plan can only hold that test by citing the owners instead of restating their work; note that §5 places no `wiring_findings` reference beside itself at all, unlike §12.
findings.text: the plan re-implements, across four sections, facts with existing owners and §5 names none of them: the section-edge resolver (`_section_scoped_edges`, roadmap.py:1079, with `_plan_section_deps` at 409), the ranking order (`priority`, roadmap.py:3514, which already orders by critical membership, sprint position, ROI and `unlocks` and which §3 rewrites rather than extends), the run classifier (`partition_live_runs`, reckon/mcp_views.py:1860), and the findings family (`_finding`, roadmap.py:1213, feeding `wiring_findings` at roadmap.py:3797)

findings.reason: a reader or agent holding the payload cannot tell which `reason` vocabulary a row carries, and §3 should either name one field for both or name and extend the existing one.
findings.text: §3 assigns every ranked row a `reason`, but a `reason` field already exists on the same `immediate_roadmap` rows at roadmap.py:3551 with plan-level text ("critical path", "sequenced after …"), and §2 says section rows are "served beside the plan rows", putting two differently-scoped `reason` values in one payload; the census of already-owned `reason` values is roadmap.py:3551 (plan rows) and the proposed §3/§7 section rows

findings.reason: five new interface families across six sections is the surface this item exists to hold to account, and the plan must state in each section's own text what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
findings.text: with cli_options at 393, mcp_views at 16 and public_definitions at 1958, §7 adds a `reckon brief --project` CLI option, a `reckon.brief.project_brief` public definition and an MCP surface, and names no option, view or definition it retires or merges, nor why nothing can be; §3, §5, §6, §9 and §12 add five wiring-finding codes (`flat-priority-signal`, `undeclared-wait`, `overlapping-scope`, `settled-link`, `redundant-link`) and a new `slug@f-id` ref form and a `descoped` declaration and §4 adds six blocking kinds in the same silence

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §2 hides the whole graph, its weights, its edges and its derived plan rows behind one function, and §7 states the brief is a composition over the §2–§5 payload rather than a second analyser.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §2, §3, §4 and §5 each re-derive a fact an existing owner already computes (`_section_scoped_edges`, `priority`, `partition_live_runs`, `_finding`) and no section names the owner it extends.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1958, cli_options 393, mcp_views 16, refusal_families 23; §7 adds a CLI option and an MCP view and §3/§5/§12 add four new wiring-finding codes and §4 adds six blocking kinds without any section naming what it retires, merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §2 adds a section graph over `plan-section-depends-on` while `reckon/roadmap.py` already resolves those entries to per-section blockers with cross-plan satisfaction, refusals and `dangling-hard-dependency` findings, and §2 cites none of that machinery.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the two genuinely thin additions, §10's refusal text and §11's `set` clause, extend their owners (`reckon/_store.py` `_PLAN_SET_TOP` and the refusal at line 2738) rather than wrapping them, and §7 justifies its composition explicitly.
